newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude steady, Dubai backwardation flattens.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude steady, Dubai backwardation flattens.

text.p: Asian crude prices were steady to weaker on Monday with Dubai backwardation flattening out close to contango after India failed to award the crude in its May buying tender.
Indian Oil Corp took five cargoes of Suez Blend from various companies at prices ranging OSP flat to plus three cents and dated Brent less $2.50 to $2.70.
The Suez Blend prices sidelined the four offers of Dubai into the IOC tender and left them hanging over the market.
In Asian trading on Monday only offers were seen for May/June Dubai at +5 cents and June/July at +10 cents.
Dubai bids were notionally assessed at -5 cents to flat in both May/June and June/July.
This compared with spreads of +7/+15 cents for May/June and +6/+12 cents for June/July on Friday in Asia before the result was known.
IOC also awarded three VLCCs of Qua Iboe at prices of BQ +60/+70 cents delivered, traders said.

The Bangchak tender had a similar affect on the Oman market after the 120,000-bpd refinery decided not to buy the crude -- generally considered its staple diet. Instead, the refinery took 750,000 barrels of Qatar's Al Shaheem from a equity producer.
A price was not heard, but the same producer sold a cargo of Al Shaheem last week at Dubai quotes +17 cents, a trader said.
Traders assessed the Oman differential at -10/-5 cents from last week's flat/-5 cents after Bangchak declined to take any of the four offers of Oman. The best offer was MPM -3 cents, traders said.
Bangchak is negotiating for regional crudes and West African grades following the tender, refinery sources said.
